newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil climbs, German demand seen strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil climbs, German demand seen strong.

text.p: NWE heating oil premiums firmed on Friday on a combination of strong German demand, Rotterdam refinery run cuts and minor production problems, traders said.
Heating oil barge premiums firmed by $1.00 to $2.00 a tonne to June IPE +$2.50/$3.50 fob Rotterdam.
Underlying IPE June gas oil futures were unchanged at $172.00 a tonne at 1140 GMT.
A major Rotterdam refiner which has been a heavy buyer all week was seen as the main bidder again on Friday morning.
A trader for the refiner said it has bought around 60,000 tonnes of material on the barge market this week, but that it had no major production problems.
"No refinery is perfect there have been a few minor difficulties in getting the blending and the specs right," the trader said.
"We are buying to meet strong demand from the market...from German end-users."
Other traders said they had heard the refinery had problems with its desulphurisation unit.
Thursday's announcement of 20 percent run cuts at Texaco's Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam in the second half of May was also helping to tighten the market.
